-78.76370,35.90670.name: UNC Fertility
-78.76370,35.90670.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Colleen Milroy, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

10.25850,53.66200.name: Kinderwunschzentrum
10.25850,53.66200.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. Operated by Universitäre Kinderwunschzentrum GmbH. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-112.76097,49.70207.name: Lethbridge Research and Development Centre
-112.76097,49.70207.status: Probationary Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, June 2024
-112.76097,49.70207.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada. Probationary Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, June 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-106.62778,52.13442.name: University of Saskatchewan
-106.62778,52.13442.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2025
-106.62778,52.13442.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, June 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

2.14400,41.39700.name: Eugin Group
2.14400,41.39700.desc: An international fertility chain operating clinics across Europe, the Americas and Asia, with cross-border treatment as a core part of the business. Patients travel to where a treatment is permitted, so a national restriction becomes a travel itinerary rather than a limit — and the chain that owns clinics on both sides of the rule is the party that benefits from the difference.

5.30500,60.39800.name: Norwegian Institute of Marine Research — spread monitoring
5.30500,60.39800.desc: The only systematic long-term monitoring anywhere of farmed salmon genetics entering wild rivers, finding introgression in a large majority of assessed populations. Nothing engineered is involved, and it is the baseline any argument about engineered salmon starts from.

-74.76000,40.22000.name: Certara / in-silico trial simulation
-74.76000,40.22000.desc: Modelling used to predict drug behaviour and increasingly to replace some trial arms with simulated controls. Fewer people receive placebo, which is a real gain, and part of the evidence for approval was produced by a model whose assumptions are commercial property.

-87.69000,42.04000.name: LanzaTech
-87.69000,42.04000.desc: Ferments engineered bacteria on industrial waste gas, turning steel-mill emissions into ethanol and chemicals at commercial plants in China, Belgium and India. Carbon capture performed by a modified organism is regulated as industrial processing rather than as biotechnology, which is why almost nobody counts it.

72.87770,19.07600.name: Rallis India
72.87770,19.07600.desc: An Indian crop protection and seeds company within the Tata group, running its own research stations and field programmes alongside a seeds business. It sits in the same position as the European agroscience contractors already on this map — generating the agronomic and efficacy data that supports a product through registration — but inside a domestic conglomerate rather than as an independent service. That difference matters for who the data belongs to: an independent contractor sells a study to whoever commissions it, while an in-house programme generates evidence for its own group's products and nobody else sees the ones that did not work.

72.87770,19.07600.name: UPL Limited
72.87770,19.07600.state: Mumbai — operations in more than 130 countries
72.87770,19.07600.desc: Founded in 1969 making red phosphorus for matches, now by its own account the fifth largest agrochemical group in the world, with revenue above five billion dollars, more than 13,600 product registrations, and an integrated portfolio running from seeds through crop protection to post-harvest. It bought Advanta Seeds in 2015 and Arysta LifeScience in 2019. The map's seed facet is built around four majors that sell traits with matching herbicides; this is a fifth company of comparable reach assembled from the other direction, by an Indian chemicals manufacturer buying its way into seed. A generic agrochemical maker acquiring a global seed business ends up in the same position as the trait owners — selling the seed and the spray together — without ever having developed a transgene.

12.56830,55.67610.name: DanBred
12.56830,55.67610.desc: The Danish pig breeding organisation, historically owned through the farmers' meat cooperative and among the largest suppliers of pig genetics worldwide. It is on this map as the cooperative case in a facet otherwise made of listed companies and family holdings: the pig genetics market is led by a British listed company and a Dutch group, and the fourth of the top four grew out of a producers' cooperative. Whether a cooperative behaves differently once it competes at that scale is the question a reader can carry to the Canadian cattle organisation and the Brazilian cotton institute elsewhere in these entries.
